note: ROUND 5: the marker finally points at the bodies. Measured at 10Hz across every live incident, percentage-empty is zero and 3 to 11 bodies sit inside the ring for the whole fuse, each individually circled. Decision density is answered — a new incident on the same tick the last one closes, every 5.9 seconds. Thumb errors are refunded completely. And the one-message grammar was verified by dumping every visible text node at 150ms intervals: for 36 straight ticks the only text on the page is the crown, then exactly two things appear, one tag and one button. TWO PRECISE DEFECTS REMAIN. The ring TELEPORTS — re-pinning snaps instead of sliding, up to 412px inside a 700ms window, so roughly one in six correctly diagnosed and correctly aimed answers is thrown away because the target moved between the button and the field. And being good at the game makes it boring: the incident filler skips elements flagged as countered, so answering well empties the screen.

pieces.name: NEST — the colony as the dashboard
pieces.judged: L11 the Depiction Law above all. Traffic, sameness, perception, possession and weather must be READABLE AS BEHAVIOUR. Seven idle ants visibly wander rather than reading idle:7. Congestion is a crowd at a doorway. History is wear on the architecture. Lineage is trail pattern. Ants get gait, posture and hesitation so a player says 'why are all five carrying the same thing' unprompted.

rounds.built: The field is a cutaway nest now, and it carries facts that used to be sentences. The score is grain filling sockets in the chamber wall. The nest is excavated live, so architecture IS history. Placing a meeting stone leaves a permanent ring of drawn stones in the wall. Strain is water: a soil tide rising from the bottom with a persistent tidemark, drowning the lower third at 100. Machine speed drops grit from the roof. A miss bursts a red shock ring and leaves hatch scars at those exact coordinates. With the lantern lit, blue intention lines fan from every ant to what it wants, and the saboteur is the one ant with no line — the whole sabotage puzzle solved visually with zero explanatory text.
rounds.gap: The tag still asserts what the picture does not show. It says 'Eight on one crumb' while thirteen ants render as a single 45px black clot you cannot count. And 5 of 17 sampled incidents had their answer ring clipped by the viewport edge, with one centred underneath the action bar — the thing you are told to tap is behind the button.

rounds.built: The nest draws the truth now: ants walking corridors, queueing nose to tail, kneeling at dig faces with spoil, resting in chambers. Unreachable chambers are drawn with a dashed outline that becomes solid the moment a tunnel arrives.
rounds.gap: The action bar OVERLAYS the nest instead of making room for it, so the bodies that ARE the incident get hidden exactly when the player is being asked to read them. The world should scale to the available height rather than being covered. Also at collapse the field carries two huge expanding shockwave rings, five small rings, two amber brackets, two scars and a paper tag at once — the exact depiction-law failure signature.

rounds.built: The world now scales to make room for the action bar instead of being covered by it, so the bodies that constitute an incident stay visible exactly when the player is asked to read them. The collapse pile-up is capped.
rounds.gap: Dash overload. Four different meanings are all encoded as dashed rings — an unreachable chamber, a rolled-back crumb, a possession scratch, and more — so the player must learn a code instead of reading a picture. In particular 'no way in' should be a DRAWN WALL, not a coded ring: stroke a sealed face of packed earth across every tunnel mouth the chamber would have, with spoil chevrons pressed against it, reusing the marks already drawn at a live dig face but mirrored inward.

pieces.name: INCIDENT — one paper tag, one action, nothing else
pieces.judged: incident then recognition then intervention. At most ONE message on screen ever. No taxonomy code during play. The six institutions become folk technology whose silhouette teaches its function: meeting stone, branching seed, tally wall, lantern, bell, threshold.

rounds.built: Incident, recognition, intervention. One paper tag near the thing, one contextual action, and nothing else — verified in the DOM at a two-incident moment: exactly one tag element, no narrator strip, no toast, no table. The action bar is absent whenever nothing is burning. The six institutions are folk technology now: meeting stone, seed, tally, lantern, bell, threshold. No two-letter code appears anywhere during play.
rounds.gap: THE EMPTY GROUND (the missing-institution incident) has no body. It is the first tag a player meets in four episodes and the second-most-fired detector in the sandbox, and at 4x zoom its ring contains nothing but two ordinary ants standing near a chamber. The fact exists only in the sentence, which is exactly what the Depiction Law forbids.

rounds.built: Incidents can now anchor on physical situations, and the field is tappable as the answer gesture: arm the meeting stone, then place it at a junction.
rounds.gap: ALL THREE CRITICS INDEPENDENTLY FOUND THE SAME THING. The incident ring is anchored to an edge midpoint rather than to the bodies that constitute the failure, and the body is only held until the tag is hung rather than for the whole fuse. So a ring reading THE JAMMED TUNNEL sits on a stretch of corridor containing ZERO ants while an obvious queue of four sits 200px outside it. The graph is real and the crowds are real, but the marker keeps pointing at the wrong place, so the picture still contradicts the sentence.

rounds.built: The marker sits on the bodies now, measured at 10Hz across every live incident: percentage-empty zero on all six chapter-4 incidents and ten of eleven in the sandbox, with a minimum of 3 to 11 bodies inside the ring for the whole fuse. Each implicated ant is individually circled. Decision density is answered: a new incident opens on the same tick the previous one closes, every 5.9 seconds, unbroken for 40 seconds. Thumb errors are completely fixed — three deliberate mis-taps left the budget at 4, 4, 4, 4 with the instrument still in hand. And L11 was verified by dumping every visible text node at 150ms intervals: for 36 consecutive ticks the only text anywhere on the page is the crown, then exactly two things appear — one tag and one button. The critic called that grammar stricter than anything in the reference work.
rounds.gap: THE RING TELEPORTS. Re-pinning snaps instantly instead of sliding, producing centre displacements of 106 to 412px inside a single 700ms window — up to 5.9 times the ring's own radius on a 390px field. A reach test that taps the ring centre after a realistic 700ms of hand travel scores 14 of 17 instead of 14 of 14 at zero lag, and every miss coincides with a jump. Roughly one in six correctly diagnosed, correctly aimed answers is thrown away because the target moved between the button and the field.

pieces.name: GUIDE — the naturalist's collection
pieces.judged: The 28-cell matrix becomes collectible plates, blank until witnessed, drawn when seen, stamped when answered. Never openable during a decision. Taxonomy as knowledge you discovered about a species, not documentation shipped with the software.

rounds.built: Highest depiction score of the round. The 28-cell matrix is gone; the taxonomy is a naturalist's collection. Each plate carries a glyph, a common name, a drawn mechanism diagram, one plain line, and the scientific code in small type at the bottom with seen, answered and missed counts plus a stamp of the institution that answered it. Uncollected plates are dashed empty slots. The guide cannot be opened while anything is burning.
rounds.gap: The first collected plate does not announce itself. Nothing flags a specimen as new until the player has already opened the drawer once, so the drawer pull first appears as a plain unlabelled box in the corner of an episode card whose dominant call to action is BEGIN. The collection mechanic is invisible at the exact moment it should hook.

pieces.name: SHELL — civic naturalism, and the abolished HUD
pieces.judged: The material/signal palette split. Quiet crown, colony-owned centre, bottom that is ABSENT unless there is a decision. Every string must have survived the Depiction Law.

rounds.built: The permanent HUD is abolished. Quiet crown, colony-owned centre, an action region that is absent rather than empty. The material/signal palette split is enforced by the build: the hex census is exactly the allowlist and nothing else. 84 detail-card lines, 12 tool blurbs, 60 narrator beats and 10 loop strings were DELETED because the colony can now be seen. What replaced them is 28 phenomenon names with one plain line each.
rounds.gap: The colony is 85 percent of the screen and completely inert to touch. Pressing MEETING STONE auto-places it at the focused incident, so the chapter-3 card that says 'put it where the trouble is' is instructing a gesture the game does not accept.

pieces.name: WORLD — 28 detectors, trade-offs, balance
pieces.judged: audit all 28 fire with working counters; section-15 trade-offs proven; misses must COST; balance measured through the live loop; and every element needs a body — a depictable behaviour the renderer can show without a caption

rounds.built: Misses now cost, and the difficulty curve is real and measured THROUGH the live loop: answering 100 percent survives 4/4 with strain 0-7; 85 percent survives with strain to 47; 70 percent survives with strain to 89; 50 percent LOSES half its runs; 30 and 0 percent lose everything. Ungoverned collapses inside 12k ticks. All six trade-offs re-verified with numbers, including truce only becoming reachable under a charter, and speed raising throughput and aggression together.
rounds.gap: The ledger/lens trade-off is the most interesting idea in the simulation and it is still a paragraph rather than something played. Stage it as an A/B passage on an identical seed: one run with only the tally, where the liar is answered but the lone dissenter is then disbelieved, and one with only the lantern, where the dissenter is heard but the rumour spreads.

rounds.built: THE NEST IS REAL, and it passes structurally rather than cosmetically. An independent geometric test that ignores the sim's own flags measured every body's distance to the nearest dug tunnel or chamber: 4720 samples across all ten chapters, worst case 12.6px from a centreline in corridors drawn 14 to 16px wide, zero ants marooned in soil in any screenshot. A single function is the only place an ant's coordinates are ever written, and it derives them from graph geometry, so it is a structural guarantee. Digging is the best thing in the build: an ant at a jagged face with spoil spraying, a tunnel stub reaching toward a chamber drawn with a dashed outline because nothing connects to it, and five seconds later the tunnel arrives, the dashes become solid, and the spoil heap stays as a permanent mark. That is siloing, depicted, with zero words. Queues are real bodies: five ants nose to tail in a one-ant tunnel.
rounds.gap: Pace overshot one way and was never tuned the other. Ants now walk watchably, answering the speed note, but the incident clock was left at a flat 900 ticks — about 19 seconds — for chapters 2 through 8. Chapter 4 produced exactly ONE decision in a 27-second run. A player can look away for twenty seconds and lose nothing, which is the precise failure the core-loop law exists to catch. Chapter 10 is correctly tuned at one decision every 3 seconds and is the proof the rest should be tuned toward it.

rounds.built: The colony moves watchably and the nest stays structurally honest. All 28 still fire, all six trade-offs still verified, audit still passing.
rounds.gap: BEING GOOD AT THE GAME MAKES IT BORING. The incident filler skips any element flagged as countered and selects on heat alone, so once the player answers correctly the sources of new incidents are suppressed and the screen goes empty. Select instead from live structural distress read straight off the nest: any crumb with three or more claims and net-zero progress, any passage with a head-on block or two or more queued, any crumb whose progress fell — and open the matching incident on that site even when the element reads as countered.

pieces.name: TEACH — the episode sequence
pieces.judged: L1 one idea at a time, L2 play first name second, L8 hands on the game within five seconds, L6 the A/B re-run, L9 the sandbox is the reward

rounds.built: Best score of the round. Hands are on the game in the first seconds instead of at 0:41. The gates are now the only place taxonomy appears, so naming lands as the payoff after the episode rather than as a prerequisite — play first, name second, done properly.
rounds.gap: Passage 10 is a sandbox you are handed rather than one you author. Give it a pre-run setup card with three dials the player sets before beginning — lineages, pace, and which three instruments they take — each drawn as its already-learned silhouette, with the seed frozen and stamped so the re-run is the player's own experiment.
